content: Selenium sulfide is a medication that functions as an anti-infective agent. It is used to alleviate itching and flaking of the scalp, as well as to remove dry, scaly particles commonly associated with dandruff or seborrheic dermatitis. Additionally, it is prescribed to treat tinea versicolor, a fungal skin infection. In some cases, it may be used for other medical purposes, so consult your doctor or pharmacist for further details. Selenium sulfide is available in a lotion form and is typically applied as a shampoo. When used as a shampoo, it is generally applied twice a week for the first two weeks, followed by once a week for an additional two to four weeks, depending on the response to treatment. For skin infections, it is usually applied once daily for seven days. Always follow the instructions provided on the packaging or prescription label, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the medication exactly as directed, and do not exceed the recommended amount or frequency. Avoid using selenium sulfide on areas of the scalp or skin that are cut or scratched. Take care to prevent the medication from coming into contact with your eyes. If accidental contact occurs, rinse your eyes thoroughly with clean water for several minutes. Do not leave selenium sulfide on your hair, scalp, or skin for extended periods, such as overnight, as it can cause irritation. This medication should not be used on children under the age of two without explicit permission from a doctor. To use selenium sulfide as a shampoo, follow these steps: 1. Remove all jewelry, as selenium sulfide can damage it. 2. Wash your hair with a regular shampoo and rinse thoroughly. 3. Shake the selenium sulfide lotion well. 4. Massage 1-2 teaspoons of the lotion into your wet scalp. 5. Leave the lotion on your scalp for 2-3 minutes. 6. Rinse your scalp three to four times with clean water. 7. Repeat steps 4, 5, and 6. 8. If you are using selenium sulfide before or after bleaching, tinting, or perming your hair, rinse your hair with cool water for at least five minutes after application to prevent discoloration. 9. Wash your hands thoroughly, including under your nails, to remove any residual lotion. If your doctor instructs you to use the lotion on your skin, apply a small amount of water to the affected area along with the lotion, and massage it to create a lather. Leave the lather on your skin for 10 minutes before rinsing it off completely. Before using selenium sulfide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to selenium sulfide or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, including vitamins, that you are currently taking. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using selenium sulfide, contact your doctor immediately. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Selenium sulfide may cause side effects. Mild side effects include oiliness or dryness of the hair and scalp, hair loss, and hair discoloration. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Severe side effects, such as scalp or skin irritation, require immediate medical attention. If you experience a serious adverse reaction, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store selenium sulfide in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. Selenium sulfide is intended for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes, nose, or mouth, and do not ingest it. Do not apply dressings, bandages, cosmetics, lotions, or other skin products to the treated area unless directed by your doctor. Do not share this medication with others. If your skin condition worsens or does not improve, inform your doctor. Keep all scheduled appointments with your healthcare provider, and consult your pharmacist if you have any questions about refilling your prescription. Selenium sulfide is available under several brand names, including: Exsel® Head and Shoulders Intensive Treatment Dandruff Shampoo® Selsun® Selsun Blue®
